# InlineEdit

InlineEdit — text that reads as text and becomes a field when it is pressed. The read view and the edit view are drawn at the same size, so opening the editor does not move anything around it. Enter or leaving the editor confirms; Escape cancels. Confirm and cancel buttons sit under the edit view and can be left off. `validate` can refuse a value with a message, and the editor stays open. The parent holds the value. `defaultValue` is what the edit view starts with each time it opens, and `onConfirm` is where the new value goes. Not for use inside a form: it saves on its own and has no say in the form's submit. Use `Input` there.

**Import:** `import { InlineEdit } from '@/components';`

## Usage

Use `InlineEdit` for a value that is read far more often than it is changed and
that can be saved on its own: a title, a name or a short note on a record or a
profile page.

Use `TextField` inside a form, where a Save button submits every field together. An
inline edit saves when it is confirmed and has no say in the form's submit, so
placing one in a form leaves two ways to save. Use a subtle `TextField` where
leaving the field should save with no buttons at all.

## Best practices

### Keep the read view plain text. {#keep-the-read-view-plain-text}

The whole read view is one button. A link or a button inside it cannot be
reached or pressed, so put those beside it.

Do: Plain text in the read view.
Don't: A link inside the read view, which cannot be reached or pressed.

### Confirm on Enter and on leaving. {#confirm-on-enter-and-on-leaving}

Both save; Escape cancels. The inline edit saves itself, so it needs no Save button of its own.

Do: Enter or leaving the field saves the title.
Don't: A separate Save step beside an inline edit.

### Use compact in dense lists. {#use-compact-in-dense-lists}

Compact draws both views 32 high, to sit in a table cell or a dense row.

Do: Compact rows in a dense list.
Don't: The default height spreads a dense list out.

### Let the parent hold the value. {#let-the-parent-hold-the-value}

`defaultValue` is what the edit view starts with each time it opens. Update it
in `onConfirm`, or the next edit starts from the old value.

### Say why a value was refused. {#say-why-a-value-was-refused}

Return the reason from `validate`, in the words a tutor would use. A refused
value leaves the editor open, so the person can fix it without retyping.

### Leave the editor open for long text. {#leave-the-editor-open-for-long-text}

Set `keepEditViewOpenOnBlur` where a stray click would publish an unfinished
thought, and keep the buttons so there is a clear way out.

## Accessibility

- **The read view is a button.** It is named by the label and the text ("Display
  name Ada Lovelace") and described as "Edit" (`editLabel`).
- **Focus follows the editor.** Opening it puts the caret in the field. Enter,
  the check or Escape returns focus to the read view. Leaving the field
  confirms and leaves focus where the person sent it.
- **Enter confirms and Escape cancels.** In a multi-line edit view, Enter adds a
  line and Cmd or Ctrl and Enter confirms.
- **Refusals are announced.** The message is in the field's caption with
  `role="alert"`, and the field is `aria-invalid`.
- **The buttons are named.** The check and the cross are icon-only, named by
  `confirmLabel` and `cancelLabel`.

## Related

- For a field in a form, use `TextField`.
- For editing in place with no buttons, use `TextField` with `appearance="subtle"`.
- For several lines edited in place, use `TextArea` with `appearance="subtle"`.

## Parts

1. **Label** (optional). Shown above both views.
2. **Read view.** The value as plain text on the field's own box. The whole view is one button.
3. **Edit view.** The field it opens into: a `TextField` in `InlineEditableTextfield`, or any edit view passed to `InlineEdit`.
4. **Actions.** The confirm and cancel icon buttons, on an overlay under the field. `hideActionButtons` leaves them off.

### States

| State | What changes |
| --- | --- |
| Rest | The read view: text on a transparent box with a transparent `--border-default` edge. |
| Hovered | The read view takes `--ds-background-neutral-subtle-hovered`. |
| Pressed | Pressing the read view opens the edit view in the same box, with the caret in it. |
| Focused | The read view draws a `--focus-ring-width` ring in `--ds-border-focused`, `--focus-ring-width` off the box. |
| Disabled | None. An inline edit has no disabled state. |
| Editing | The field's fill and `--border-default` input edge appear; nothing else moves. |
| Invalid | The field stays open with the danger edge and the message in its caption. |
| Placeholder | An empty read view shows the placeholder in `--ds-text-subtlest`. |

### Tokens

| Part | Token |
| --- | --- |
| Read view height | 40: `--height-250`. Compact 32: `--item-height-md`. |
| Read view box | `--radius-0625`, a `--border-default` transparent edge, `--pad-x-md` either side. |
| Read view text | `--body-default` in `--ds-text`; placeholder `--ds-text-subtlest`. |
| Read view hovered | `--ds-background-neutral-subtle-hovered`. |
| Actions | `--ds-surface-overlay` with `--ds-shadow-overlay`, `--radius-md`, `--stack-sm` padding and gap. |
| Gap under the label | `--stack-sm`. |

The edit view takes the field's own tokens: see Text field.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Label the value it holds: "Display name". | Label the action: "Edit name". |
| Give an empty value a placeholder that says what to add: "Add a nickname". | Leave an empty read view blank, with nothing to press. |
| Say why a value was refused: "Enter a name." | "Invalid" or "Error". |

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Description |
|------|------|---------|-------------|
| `id` | string | — | Base id for the edit view's control; the label points at it while editing. |
| `label` | node | — | Shown above both views. |
| `defaultValue` | any | — | What the edit view starts with each time it opens. The parent updates it after a confirm. |
| `readView` | func (required) | — | Returns the read view's content. Keep it to plain text: the whole view is one button. |
| `editView` | func (required) | — | Returns the edit view, given `{ id, value, onChange, validation, validationMessage, isSaving }`. `onChange` takes a value or a change event. |
| `onConfirm` | func | — | Called with the value on Enter, on leaving the editor and on the confirm button. Throw or reject to keep the editor open with the error. |
| `onCancel` | func | — | Called when Escape or the cancel button closes the editor. |
| `onEdit` | func | — | Called when the editor opens. |
| `validate` | func | — | Returns a message to refuse the value, or nothing to accept it. May be async. |
| `keepEditViewOpenOnBlur` | bool | `false` | Leaving the editor no longer confirms; only Enter and the confirm button do. |
| `startWithEditViewOpen` | bool | `false` | Opens in the edit view and puts the caret in it. |
| `hideActionButtons` | bool | `false` | Leaves off the confirm and cancel buttons. Enter, Escape and leaving the editor still work. |
| `compact` | bool | `false` | The 24 height, with the compact buttons. |
| `readViewFitContainerWidth` | bool | `false` | The read view fills its container, so the whole row is one press target. |
| `editLabel` | string | `'Edit'` | What a screen reader hears after the read view, naming what pressing does. |
| `confirmLabel` | string | `'Confirm'` | — |
| `cancelLabel` | string | `'Cancel'` | — |
| `className` | string | `''` | — |
